title: The Goedel numbering of first-order formulas is injective
statement: FO.Formula.code assigns to every first-order formula a natural number -- FO.Code.pair tag payload, one distinct tag for each of the nine constructors, with FO.Term fields coded through FO.Term.code and the payload nesting to the right -- and the assignment is injective: if two formulas have the same code they are the same formula.

formal.statement: theorem FO.Formula.code_injective : ((x0 : FO.Formula) -> ((x1 : FO.Formula) -> ((x2 : Eq.{1} AxNat (FO.Formula.code x0) (FO.Formula.code x1)) -> Eq.{1} FO.Formula x0 x1)))

evidence.supports: FO.Formula.code_injective is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement, and rests on no axiom. It is a double recursion -- an outer FO.Formula.rec at the motive 'forall q, code p = code q -> p = q', with an inner FO.Formula.rec case analysis on q -- so the recursors' arities fix 9 x 9 = 81 cases and a skipped case is not possible.
evidence.notes: Declared in crates/axeyum-lean-kernel/src/fo_numbering.rs by declare_code_injective, the same builder that produces FO.Term.code_injective; the two differ only in the constructor table they are handed. The checker fails on absence.

evidence.supports: The theorem's INFERRED type is rebuilt in the test module from FO.Formula.code and Eq and compared by Kernel::def_eq, with the CONVERSE ('p = q -> code p = code q', true but congruence rather than injectivity) as the negative control: the two must NOT be def_eq.
evidence.notes: Without this row the fact would rest on a rendered string nobody compared against a rebuilt term.

evidence.supports: FO.Formula.code is a Definition; admission says nothing about what it computes. Five formula codes are pinned by Kernel::def_eq against hand-computed numerals -- bot |-> 0, eqf (var 0) (var 0) |-> 2, imp bot bot |-> 27, all bot |-> 35, ex bot |-> 44. The separating controls are chosen at the two places a copy-paste between cases would collapse the numbering and nothing else would notice: all versus ex (same arity, same field), and the three binary connectives against each other.
evidence.notes: These codes are small only because the pairing is the anti-diagonal one (F:fo-code-pairing-round-trip); every numeral in this kernel is unary, so under a 2^a (2b+1) pairing 'all bot' would not normalize inside a test at all and this row could not exist.

evidence.supports: MUTATION-VERIFIED. Two mutations were applied to a scratch copy of the lane's worktree, built, run, and restored byte-for-byte with git status verified clean. Both are recorded with their measured kill counts in docs/plan/status/arithmetization-2026-09-05.md rather than here, so this row does not repeat a number it did not measure itself.

notes:
HOW THE 81 CASES CLOSE, in two shapes. The 72 OFF-diagonal cases are one construction: FO.Code.pair_inj_left reads the two tags off the hypothesis, and distinct unary numerals are refuted by stripping succs with Nat.succ_injective until Nat.succ_ne_zero applies. The 9 diagonal cases peel the payload with pair_inj_left/pair_inj_right, convert each component -- a Nat field is already an equality, an FO.Term field goes through FO.Term.code_injective, a recursive field through the induction hypothesis -- and recombine by congruence one argument at a time.

WHY THE PAIRING'S ROUND TRIP HAD TO COME FIRST. Proving 'pair a b = pair c d -> a = c' directly would be a double induction with a Nat-level case split inside it, once per component. Through FO.Code.fst_pair/snd_pair each direction is three Eq steps, and that is what makes 97 syntax-level cases affordable rather than 97 nested inductions.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. It is NOT a decidable equality on FO.Formula: from code p = code q one gets p = q, but nothing here decides whether code p = code q, because that would need a decidable equality on Nat applied at codes plus a decoder. It is also NOT representability: no syntactic OPERATION is shown to be an arithmetic function, because that needs a decoder Nat -> FO.Formula. Both gaps are the single open fact F:fo-formula-decoder.
